summary: Alfred Horsford Bingley was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He was educated at Kensington School and studied at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst from around 1884 to 1885.

Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Bonn (1886-1890). He held posts at Bonn (~1895-1899), Greifswald (~1899-1903), Basel (~1903-1906), Giessen (~1906-1914), Freiburg (~1914-1917), and Leipzig (~1917-1934).

Alfred Louis Noël de Sadous was an Indologist who earned his dr.-ès-lettres from the University of Paris by 1847, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He served as a teacher ("professor") at troisième at Lycée Hoche.

Alfred Ludwig worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Berlin under Müller, Weber, Boller, Bonitz, Boeckh, and Haupt. After habilitating at Vienna in 1858, he was a professor at Charles University from 1860 to 1901.

Indologist and linguist Alfred Master studied at Epsom College and Oxford (D.Phil.). He lectured at SOAS (1937-1939, 1944-1950; Governing Body 1952-1960) and served as Assistant Keeper at the India Office Records (1951-1957).

Philosopher Alfred North Whitehead was educated at Sherborne School and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic positions at the University of Cambridge (1884-1910), Imperial College London (1914-1924), and Harvard University (1924-1937).

Alfred Nottrott worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Leipzig, also serving as a missionary with the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church from 1867.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at King Edward's School and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers. He later held posts at the University of Sydney (~1926-1931), University of Chicago (~1931-1937), Oxford (~1937-1946), and São Paulo (~1942-1944).

Alfred Roussel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Saint-Malo, the Major Seminary of Rennes, and under Abel Bergaigne and Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Fribourg (1903-1920).

Linguist Alfred Schmitt studied at Gnadenfeld Seminary and the University of Rostock under Gustav Herbig and Hermann Güntert. He held posts at Rostock (1928-1935), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1935-1941), and the University of Münster (1941-1956).

Alfred Shenington Geden worked in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies, holding degrees from Oxford and Aberdeen. He was Principal of Royapettah College (1886-1889) and taught at Richmond College (~1891-1922) and Wesleyan College (1891-1915).

Alfred William Stratton, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Toronto and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held positions at Chicago (1895-1899), Oriental College (Principal, 1899), and the University of the Punjab (~1899-1902).

Alfred von Gutschmid worked in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology, studying at Leipzig and Bonn under Christian Lassen. He held professorships at Kiel (1863-1873), Königsberg (1873), Jena (1876), and Tübingen (1877).
Linguist Alfredo Trombetti studied at the University of Bologna from ~1887 to 1891. He spent his career there as Professor of Semitic Philology from 1904 and Professor of Glottology from 1912.
Ali Beth was an Indologist who completed doctoral studies at Utrecht University between ~1937 and 1943 under the supervision of Jan Gonda.
Ali S. Asani is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1973-1984). He became a professor at Harvard University around 2008.

Linguist Alice Harris studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~1970-1971) and Harvard University (~1971-1976). She later held faculty posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979-2009) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

Alice Margaret Stevenson was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Somerville College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, later earning degrees from Trinity College Dublin and the University of Oxford.
Alice Y. Tseng is a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied as a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2013).

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (2000-2009), supervised by Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and became an Associate Professor at York University in 2009.
